TSMC is finally set to resume SRAM scaling with its A14 node, following a stall that began after N5, according to Korean media reports.

SRAM bitcell sizes have remained at 0.021 µm² for roughly eight years since the introduction of the N5 (5 nm) process in 2020. With A14, however, the size of a high-density 6T SRAM (static random-access memory) bitcell is expected to shrink to below 0.017 µm².

Korean media noted that this would put TSMC ahead of Intel’s 18A process, for which Intel reported a high-density bitcell size of 0.021 µm² and a maximum SRAM macro density of 38.1 megabits/mm² at last year’s ISSCC.

SRAM is the ultrafast cache memory used inside CPUs, GPUs, and AI accelerators. Smaller bitcells—the smallest individual memory cells—allow more memory to fit into the same area, directly affecting performance and power efficiency.

Arguably the most valuable insight from the past few days of memory industry news came from Lam Research CEO Tim Archer.

On the company’s October 21, 2026 earnings call, Archer explained that the growing adoption of SLC NAND for AI could increase the wafer capacity needed to supply the same amount of storage. Let’s take a closer look.

Specifically, moving from TLC to SLC-class products reduces the number of bits stored per cell to roughly one-third. As a result, he said, every 1-percentage-point increase in SLC’s share of total NAND bits would require approximately 2% more wafer capacity to meet the same overall bit demand.

Some readers may wonder whether SLC is an outdated approach to NAND production, used mainly in legacy products.

Far from it. SLC is a highly promising area that could play a role in NAND similar to the one HBM plays in DRAM.

NAND customers, including NVIDIA and the hyperscalers, are developing next-generation products based on SLC. Within the NVIDIA ecosystem, the focus is on SLC-based XL-Flash, also known as high-IOPS NAND. Outside the NVIDIA ecosystem, SLC is also being used as the basis for HBF.

Put simply, matching the storage capacity of one TLC wafer requires roughly three SLC wafers, while matching one QLC wafer requires roughly four. As production of these SLC-based products ramps up, they will consume an increasing amount of NAND wafer capacity. Just as HBM drove shortages in DRAM, these products could create a similar dynamic in NAND.

With HBF and XL-Flash scheduled to enter volume production in 2028 and 2027, respectively, I think we should consider whether some analysts’ forecasts of NAND prices beginning to decline in the fourth quarter of 2027 may be overly conservative.

The selloff continues. Next, I’m shifting from shorting beta to shorting alpha. I call it the “reverse bottleneck trade”—the counterpart to the earlier bottleneck trade.

The logic is simple: AI demand will keep growing, but that growth may slow, while upstream suppliers keep expanding capacity in response to shortages and fat margins. Once effective supply catches up with demand, bargaining power shifts back downstream. During a shortage, customers care first about availability. Good enough will do. Once supply is plentiful, they start comparing performance, cost, power consumption, and reliability again. That’s when we find out who wins orders on competitiveness and who was simply picking up overflow because the leaders couldn’t supply enough.

My watchlist includes memory runner-up MU, second- and third-tier optical players COHR and AAOI, and foundry runner-up INTC.

This trade doesn’t even require the AI bubble to burst. Supply growth just needs to start outpacing demand growth. I think there’s a very high probability these stocks put in an “Everest chart” over the next year—a towering peak followed by a collapse back down. If you don’t have the stomach to go all-in on outright shorts, anti-bottleneck pair trades are another good way to express the view: long LITE / short AAOI; long TSM / short INTC; long NVDA / short AMD or AVGO.

【美股复盘 · 10月26日】

**大市**

美股周一全线造好，四大指数同步收高，以科网股为首的纳指表现最为突出。纳指ETF $QQQ 收报712.20，升1.11%，升幅居四大之首；标普500ETF SPY 收报765.37，升0.71%；罗素小型股ETF IWM 收报276.97，升0.44%；道指ETF DIA 收报522.97，升0.31%，相对落后，反映资金明显偏向成长及科技一端，而非传统工业金融权重。市宽配合指数方向，106只观察股中70只上升、36只下跌，上升股数约为下跌股数的两倍，升势并非仅靠少数超大型权重股拉动。反向杠杆产品全日沽压沉重，做空半导体的 SOXS 急泻8.54%，做空纳指的 SQQQ 挫3.28%，两者跌幅均数倍于相应指数的升幅，侧面印证日内走势反复有限、升幅守得较稳。

**板块**

光通讯及网络设备股一枝独秀，升幅榜近乎被该板块包揽： LITE 暴升8.19%，为全日表现最佳的观察股； AAOI 升6.56%； COHR 升5.83%； CIEN 升4.89%；通讯设备商 NOK 亦升6.14%。半导体设计方面， ARM 升6.19%，为板块内的领涨大型股。电力及能源设备同步造好，燃料电池股 BE 升5.49%。软件股中，数据库供应商 MDB 升4.86%。此外，防务股 LMT 升5.13%，电动车股 TSLA 升5.21%。

沽压则集中于数字资产相关、消费及医药一端，与大市方向背驰。 CRCL 重挫7.07%；加密货币交易平台 COIN 跌2.95%；经纪商 HOOD 跌2.35%，三者同日失色。流媒体股 NFLX 跌2.96%，药业股 MRK 跌3.21%，零售股 TGT 跌2.77%。拉丁美洲数字银行 NU 单日暴泻16.95%，为全日跌幅最大的观察股，表现与整体升市完全脱节。

**焦点**

盘面以外，市场全日的核心议题仍是算力供给的硬约束。亚马逊管理层表示，AWS 2027年的容量已「基本卖光」。卖光本身是需求强劲的证据，但同时意味着该年度的收入上限不再由需求决定，而是由变压器、涡轮机以及何时通电决定；在全行业同时排队的环境下，工期滑一个季度未必只是递延，客户随时转投手上有现成机位的同业。此一叙事的受益方向，与今日光通讯、网络设备及电力设备股的相对强势一致。

融资端的分化亦值得留意。 META 已递交一份不披露规模的 mixed shelf，先将随时发债发股的额度挂上；与此同时，债券市场对缺乏AI数据中心以外收入来源的发行人态度明显收紧。长端利率高企之下，能够顺利融资的往往是最不缺钱的一批，真正缺钱的反而被关在门外——此为未来AI资本开支叙事的主要风险点。

一级市场方面，Anthropic已递交在纳斯达克上市的申请文件，招股书同时列明其技术对人类构成灾难性、生存层面风险的风险提示。此类表述在法律上属标准免责安排，惟就「生存层面风险」一项而言，其现实约束力有限，料成日后定价争议所在。

能源物流方面，沙特近期在新加坡租用油罐储货，等同在油价仍处高位时主动把现货搬到亚洲买家门口；相同手法十余年前曾在冲绳使用。供应方一边维持掐紧水龙头的叙事，一边替客户修通最后一公里管道，此举对后市原油定价权的含义，值得长线留意。

**小结**

全日为一次由科网及算力硬件主导、市宽配合的普涨，惟升势内部分化鲜明：受益于数据中心基建的光通讯、网络设备与电力设备股明显跑出，而数字资产相关、医药及零售则遭沽压。两只反向杠杆产品的跌幅，确认日内并无明显回吐压力。分析指，后市关键在于 QQQ 能否站稳712水平，以及上升股数能否持续维持在七十只以上；若升势继续由单一板块独力支撑，而市宽转弱，则需提防高位反复偏软。卖方对个别大型科技股的目标价区间分歧已明显扩大，亦反映市场对AI资本开支的盈利路径尚未形成共识。
